analysis:
Examined the MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift head excerpts (lines 530-1554). The only changed lines are 833-835, which pass `promptCacheScope: cacheEnabled ? requestCacheScope : nil` into ProviderPromptContractPipeline.tokenize. That follows the T-041 posture: the coordinator-authored cache scope is derived from authenticated account, model build and prompt contract, and callers cannot override it. It is nil when the cache is disabled, so prompt-token reuse is partitioned exactly like the KV prefix cache, and this does not widen cross-tenant sharing. I did not see the PromptTokenCache implementation, so I could not confirm that the scope actually keys its entries. A reviewer should check that no token-cache lookup ignores the scope, and that the token cache stores no plaintext prompt-derived data on disk; that would be a new at-rest artifact under T-041 leak #2 and A-001.

The media path (lines 530-809) and the event-stream code are unchanged context. Fail-closed behavior is preserved: the forced tool_choice refusal, the media gate release on every exit, and the no-bridge hard error.

The new ChatTemplateLoopRewrites.swift (patch, 156 lines) does verbatim string-block replacements of chat templates (Gemma 4, GPT-OSS) for linear-time rendering. Each rewrite requires exactly one match and refuses if the introduced variable names already occur in the template. The env flag DARKBLOOM_TTFT_TEMPLATE_LOOPS only disables it. The excerpt is truncated, but the visible logic looks fail-safe; a mismatch returns nil and keeps the original template. The header says the render is compared against the unchanged template at load and in sampled checks, but that verification code is not in the supplied units.

Residual risk is semantic: a rewrite that diverges from the original could alter prompts, an integrity concern rather than a confidentiality one. The untrusted templates come from model files (A-004, T-012). Rewrites are string-only and add no code execution beyond the Jinja already in use. Not verified: PromptTokenCache, the tokenize signature change, and caller wiring in unchanged files.
